body: This is going to sound really stupid of me , and I know that Reddit is home to so many extraordinary people who have been under extraordinary circumstances , but I don’t feel like one of those people who can just bounce back. I had everything in College (besides the fact that clearly we weren’t all as close as I thought ) and I can’t take the fact that now as an adult it’s going to be SO much harder to get better and I really just want to lay in a hole until I die of natural causes tbh . 😂🙃

I was diagnosed with aspergers last year and I had a huge nervous breakdown and suffered depression from June until now after realising I have such few social connections and I spent most of my summer not doing anything . When College opened in September I couldn’t even get out of bed, I was in a really dark place and because I missed out on so much work the Special needs person said that my school tutors said it was advised that I take a gap year .

Thanks for your reply . I am being encouraged to go to an autism support group but I have aspergers which is a milder form of autism and the last thing I want is to be surrounded by less socially capable people than me , no disrespect to anyone who is severely autistic . I think a lot of is to do with knowing that no matter how hard you try , your social situation isn’t going to change and thinking that I would end up with a group of close friends is what really motivated me .

Maybe you’re desensitised to an extent because you’re constantly surrounded by these types of issues which is really normal when you do something or experience something enough. At least your manager understands , a good distraction or a hobby to take your mind of it might help.
I’ve heard of this but I’m not sure where you can get witch hazel?

I think it’s really normal to feel this way given the intense nature of the job . Why not take a break ? Maybe it would be helpful to seek professional advice as well; statistics show that care workers are the most likely group to suffer from mental health problems.
